summary: Verified the audio-mixing fix in /app/frontend/src/sound.ts. TEST 1 (code review) PASS: setAudioModeAsync({ interruptionMode: 'mixWithOthers' }).catch(() => {}) is invoked exactly once at module load (line 7), wrapped in .catch for web safety; playSound still lazily creates and reuses AudioPlayer instances via the players cache. TEST 2 (runtime smoke) PASS: logged in as tester1@belote.tn at viewport 1600x738, navigated to /game/local_short_soundtest1, announced a 160-spades bid ([data-testid=bid-suit-S] + [data-testid=bid-value-160] + [data-testid=announce-bid-button]) and played 3 cards (KH, QH, JH) with your-turn-pill visible — deal/card/trick sounds fired through playSound with ZERO uncaught errors in console/pageerror matching audio|AudioModule|setAudioModeAsync|expo-audio. Only an expected browser autoplay-policy warning appeared ('play() failed because the user didn't interact with the document first'), which is caught by the try/catch inside playSound and is explicitly listed as acceptable in the review request. TEST 3 (regression) PASS: after login the app routed to /home and rendered the home grid (home-screen, home-grid, play-online-card, play-solo-card, learn-card, private-game-card) — the module-level setAudioModeAsync call did NOT crash startup. Minor script note: I initially looked for [data-testid=tab-profile] to flip the sound switch, but this app uses a home grid (no tab bar), so I skipped it; sound defaults to enabled=true in sound.ts and audio was clearly attempted during play (proven by the autoplay warning), confirming the code path was exercised. No regressions detected; the fix is safe for merge and the mixWithOthers behavior can only be end-to-end validated on a physical iOS/Android device as noted in the request.
action_items: None from this iteration — audio-focus fix is verified error-free on web preview. Recommend a manual physical-device check (Android in particular) to confirm background music from another app is no longer paused when SFX play.
critical_code_review_comments: sound.ts fix is minimal and correct: single module-level setAudioModeAsync call, .catch guard for web (where the module can no-op or reject), AudioPlayer cache untouched.

Sound is enabled by default (let enabled = true) before AsyncStorage resolves — acceptable for smoke testing; if the user had previously disabled sound, the very first playSound after cold start could still fire once until AsyncStorage resolves (pre-existing behavior, not caused by this fix).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Auth testIDs on /auth are auth-email-input / auth-password-input / auth-submit-button (NOT login-*). Post-login lands on /home with a grid (home-screen), no bottom tab bar — profile is opened from menu-button, not a tab-profile testID. Local offline games at /game/local_short_<anything> work without WS. Bid flow: bid-suit-{S|H|D|C} + bid-value-{80..160} + announce-bid-button. Cards use [data-testid^='hand-card-'] with aria-disabled='true' when unplayable; your-turn-pill signals your turn. Browser autoplay warning 'play() failed because the user didn't interact...' is expected on web and is silently swallowed by playSound's try/catch — do NOT treat it as a bug.
rca_of_issue: Original bug: SFX in the game paused the user's background music on other apps because expo-audio's default audio mode requests exclusive audio focus. Fix (verified): calling setAudioModeAsync({ interruptionMode: 'mixWithOthers' }) once at sound.ts module load switches Android to no-audio-focus mode and iOS to mixing category, so SFX now play alongside the user's music. Web-safety: wrapped in .catch since expo-audio's web shim may reject/no-op. Reproduction on physical device: start music in another app -> open Belote game -> play any card -> external music should continue uninterrupted. Full end-to-end validation requires a physical device (web preview cannot host system-level audio focus).
